extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners reviewing Office action practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for identifying claim limitations subject to 35 U.S.C. §112(f) (pre‑AIA §112 sixth paragraph), establishing the broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI), and documenting the interpretation in an Office action using the new USPTO form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for § 112(f) interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: When an element or step is claimed only by its function, § 112(f) interpretation is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application of § 112(f) is driven by the claim language (not applicant intent). § 112(f) is a claiming style permitted only for claims that recite a combination of elements (not single-element claims). Analyze each limitation/element individually; if a limitation claims only a function and no sufficient structure/material/act is recited, interpret that limitation under § 112(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: MPEP 2181 three-prong test for identifying § 112(f) limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply § 112(f) to a claim limitation if it meets the following 3-prong test: (A) the claim limitation uses the term “means” or “step” or a term used as a substitute for “means” that is a generic placeholder (also called a nonce term or a non-structural term having no specific structural meaning) for performing the claimed function; (B) the term “means” or “step” or the generic placeholder is modified by functional language, typically, but not always linked by the transition word “for” (e.g., “means for”) or another linking word or phrase, such as "configured to" or "so that"; and (C) the term “means” or “step” or the generic placeholder is not modified by sufficient structure, material, or acts for performing the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all three prongs are satisfied, interpret the limitation under § 112(f). If the test is not met, interpret the limitation under its plain meaning in light of the specification (MPEP 2111). When in doubt, establish a reasoned position on the record explaining the analysis (words of the claim, specification, state of the art) so applicant may respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption when 'means' or 'step' is absent
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim limitation that does not use the term “means” or “step” creates a rebuttable presumption that the claim limitation is not interpreted under § 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is rebutted when the limitation recites function without reciting sufficient structure/material/acts to entirely perform that function (e.g., a generic placeholder like 'device' coupled with a function). When rebutted, document that § 112(f) is being applied (use FP 7.30.06). Note that this presumption is rarely overcome for process claim limitations that do not use the word 'step.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption when 'means' or 'step' is present
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim limitation that explicitly uses the term “means” or “step” creates a rebuttable presumption that the claim limitation is interpreted under § 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is rebutted when the limitation recites sufficient structure/material/acts to entirely perform the recited function (for example, 'a printer means for printing' where 'printer' is a recognized structure). When rebutted, document that § 112(f) is not being used (use FP 7.30.07). Remember § 112(f) is pertinent only where a function is recited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic placeholders (terms standing in for 'means')
rubrics_metrics.description: Other words often stand in for 'means' (generic placeholders) — e.g., 'mechanism', 'device', 'unit', 'module' — but there is no exhaustive list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specification and the perspective of one of ordinary skill in the art to decide whether the word denotes a reasonably well-understood structure or is merely a non-structural placeholder. The presence of such a generic word does not automatically invoke § 112(f); analyze under the three-prong test and explain the basis on the record when § 112(f) is applied or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between means-plus-function and step-plus-function
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Means-plus-function' limitations refer to structural elements and can appear in product or process claims; 'step-plus-function' limitations recite a step in purely functional terms and will appear in process claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step-plus-function limitations are rare because inclusion of action words (specific acts) typically rebuts the presumption that § 112(f) applies. Courts have not extended the generic-placeholder doctrine to 'step' as readily as to 'means'; treat step analyses accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing the Broadest Reasonable Interpretation (BRI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish the BRI of both § 112(f) and non-§ 112(f) claim limitations before examining for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BRI of a § 112(f) limitation is limited to what is disclosed in the specification (structure) and equivalents that perform the recited function. The BRI of a non-§ 112(f) limitation is its plain meaning in light of the specification (unless a special definition/disclaimer applies). After establishing BRI, proceed to examine §§ 101, 102, 103, 112, and non-statutory double patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to record claim interpretation in an Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of § 112(f) should appear toward the beginning of an Office action under the 'CLAIM INTERPRETATION' heading; § 112(f) controls interpretation but is not a basis for a rejection by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address § 112(f) when a limitation is first interpreted under it (typically in the first Office action or when the limitation is first introduced). Once established on the record, repetition is unnecessary unless the interpretation changes. Use the Claim Interpretation heading also for other clarifying claim-interpretation remarks or special definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of new form paragraphs to make § 112(f) interpretation on the record
rubrics_metrics.description: New form paragraphs assist examiners in establishing § 112(f) claim interpretation and explaining presumptions: FP 7.30.05 (BRI under § 112(f), three-prong test, presumptions); FP 7.30.06 (§ 112(f) invoked despite absence of 'means'); FP 7.30.07 (§ 112(f) not invoked despite presence of 'means'); plus FP 7.30.03.h (Claim Interpretation Header) and FP 7.30.03 (Statutory Basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate FP(s) via the Claim Interpretation tab in OACS/OC. When invoking § 112(f) without 'means', include FP 7.30.06 and identify the claim(s)/limitation(s); when 'means' is present but rebutted, include FP 7.30.07 and identify the limitation(s). Use FP 7.30.05 to state the three-prong test and presumptions. Examiners can append brief explanatory remarks after the form paragraph inserts (e.g., 'In this application the recited "module" for printing has no structural meaning').

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and level of explanation to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions should provide sufficient explanation whenever prosecution positions and claim-interpretation decisions can be clarified for applicant and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond inserting form paragraphs, consider adding reasons why particular subject matter is allowable, whether priority documents provide support, identifying terms not given their plain meaning, noting unsupported breadth of claim terms, and identifying § 112(f) language. If multiple instances of the same generic placeholder occur, a single clarifying statement may address all instances and list claims where § 112(f) interpretation applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper responses by applicant to avoid § 112(f) interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriate applicant response to avoid interpretation under § 112(f): amend the claim limitation to clearly recite a definite structure, material, or act that entirely performs the recited function; or present a sufficient showing that the limitation already recites such a structure/material/act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant amends to add a named structure or demonstrates that the claim already recites sufficient structure/acts, the presumption that § 112(f) applies may be rebutted; the examiner should then document the rebuttal (e.g., FP 7.30.07) and re-evaluate BRI and patentability accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper responses by applicant to obtain § 112(f) interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriate applicant response to obtain interpretation under § 112(f): amend the claim limitation to remove the structure/material/act that performs the recited function; or present a sufficient showing that the claim does not recite any structure/material/act that entirely performs the recited function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant removes or shows absence of structure performing the function, the limitation may meet the three-prong test and be interpreted under § 112(f); examiners should document invocation (FP 7.30.06) and limit BRI to specification-disclosed structure and equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation-by-limitation analysis with illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: § 112(f) analysis is performed on a limitation-by-limitation basis; examples illustrate common outcomes (e.g., 'knife blade' is a named structure -> not § 112(f); 'means for cutting' -> § 112(f) and limited to spec-disclosed spoon-with-knife-blade; 'device for cutting' (generic placeholder) -> § 112(f); 'knife blade means for cutting' (means present but structure recited) -> presumption rebutted -> not § 112(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete examples from the specification when explaining why a limitation meets or fails the three-prong test. Identify specific claim language in the Office action and, where helpful, include short explanatory remarks showing how the specification supports the structural disclosure (e.g., motor disclosed for 'mechanism...for rotating', spring disclosed for 'unit ... for biasing').
